## 01 — Level fantasy and player experience

A six-axis factory robot has passed its drive-stage commissioning but cannot be trusted to navigate by sight. The player receives the **PNX-29 perception motherboard** and must construct, test and repair a four-camera, LiDAR/ToF, IMU and timing/control pipeline. No robot arm, external lab room, physical optical bench or physical meter mesh should be imported; this package is board-only and should reuse the existing workshop and world-space virtual instruments.

The core educational difference is **sensor presence ≠ valid timestamp ≠ calibrated measurement ≠ good fusion ≠ independent authorization**. Healthy LEDs, a green stereo view, or an illustrative point cloud must never automatically certify perception safety.

**Expected AAA-style presentation:** premium dark-blue/teal solder mask, anodized heatsinks, gold contacts, detailed BGA and passives, restrained scientific holograms, scene-local highlights and VFX, coherent stereo/point-cloud visualizations, audible diagnostic cues through existing Project Spark voice systems, readable high-contrast data, mouse/touch parity and deterministic replayable QA. These are target behaviors and integration requirements, **not claims about systems already present in the art package**.

## 06 — Timing, sensor processing, frame data and bounded fusion

Design the runtime as separate **Source Truth Layer** (Project Spark electrical and component state), **Perception Evidence Layer** (validated acquisition), and **Display/Character Layer** (holographic visuals and voice). The latter can never write certified truth.

- **Cameras A–D:** track actual required power/clock/reset/connector continuity; use frame sequence IDs, valid timestamps (units microseconds or nanoseconds with clearly defined epoch), frame CRC, link quality, valid exposure and optional calibration revision. Stereo pair A/B and depth pair C/D; do not infer valid disparity from arbitrary colored art. Each missing/corrupt camera invalidates dependent fusion evidence.
- **LiDAR/ToF:** a separate range-measurement channel with acquisition time, echo/quality validity, range uncertainty, supply-ripple sensitivity and a deterministic educational point-cloud test fixture. The visualization must be labelled synthetic until real sensor modeling is bound.
- **IMU:** independently timestamped angular rate and acceleration with bias/noise calibration, consistent coordinate frame and plausible time/units.
- **Synchronizer:** independent clock reference and PPS-like/frame-trigger distribution, measured skew and jitter; reject stale/out-of-order samples, timestamp wraps, missed triggers and incompatible clock epochs. Source model must be qualified first.
- **Fusion:** match synchronized sets within explicit configurable acceptance windows, transform measurements into a common calibrated frame, propagate confidence/uncertainty, gate false positives and enforce replayable accepted/rejected frame decisions. The specific rates, tolerances, depth accuracy and FOV must be data-driven and unapproved until sensor-source authority is supplied.
- **Safety:** independent protected-perception gate; valid perception score alone must never release robot motion or imply rated real-world autonomy. Only an approved independently supervised state may permit protected game actions.

Provide deterministic fixtures for missing camera, stale packets, LiDAR dropout, duplicate frames, jitter bursts, invalid extrinsics, confidence collapse and sensor-clock drift. Separate per-tick simulation from renderer/UI refresh; no allocation-heavy global searches in `Update`. The shipped `SparkL121PerceptionFusionTeachingDemo` is illustrative and non-scoring; keep it isolated.

## 07 — Three recoverable physical faults

**F1 — Camera 2 differential receive-via intermittency.** A specific approved via/contact intermittently opens under a reproducible seed. This must change the conductive graph and the camera frame validation path; camera A can remain healthy but stereo pairing must fail when B is invalid. Use existing world-space net tracer, oscilloscope and continuity repair. Require fresh calibration and stereo replay after the actual contact repair. The source currently has no approved via assignment, so the target is **UNASSIGNED**.

**F2 — PPS/frame-trigger distribution drift.** A specific approved timing component/contact causes increased clock skew or jitter. Timestamp residuals grow and the fusion gate rejects stale pairings. Diagnose with virtual differential timing tools; after authorized repair, acquire fresh clock evidence and rerun synchronized fusion. The source does not identify approved package pins.

**F3 — LiDAR/ToF 5 V filter capacitor ESR degradation.** A real component parameter must change under the existing electrical solver so supply ripple or transient sag affects LiDAR ranging and confidence. Repair with correct capacitor value/package/solder state; rerun voltage and range tests. The source does not identify the real capacitor ref or net. Do not fabricate it.

For F1–F3, record unique fault ID, physical component/pin/via target, source revision, fault seed, topology generation, tool, accepted repair mutation and new evidence IDs. Wrong tool, target, power precondition or stale evidence must produce an actionable error rather than awarding progress.

Then supervised removal must actually open this independent signal, invalidate its freshness, latch protected-operation inhibition, and prevent relevant robot actions **without fictitiously zeroing unrelated powered rails**. Reconnect a real mapped terminal path; require independent fresh power/clock, camera, LiDAR, IMU, synchronization and fusion evidence; require an explicit reset and renewed authorization. A level-complete screen, fixed HIGH pin, cosmetic jumper or prior healthy sample must never substitute. If missing physical pin mapping, block O6 and state why.

To unlock real gameplay and six certified objectives, obtain these approved design artifacts:

1. Pin-mapped 280-part BOM with values and independently verified 3D footprints, orientation, pin-one and legal solder pads.
2. All 368 route task pad endpoints and net IDs, factory-copper flags, route classes, widths, clearances, signal pairs and exact one-or-more allowed layers.
3. All 140 via net IDs, drilling types and legal start/end layer spans for the validated 34-layer stack-up.

5. Protected input and low-noise 5 V/3.3 V rails, sensor clock/reset sequencing and safe-current constraints.
6. Approved camera frame sizes, rates, link/serializer models, calibration and expected stereo baseline; LiDAR and IMU profile/coordinate units.
7. Timing reference architecture, PPS/frame trigger source, valid skew/jitter budget, replay fixtures and calibrated confidence thresholds.
8. Project Spark's actual solver/terminal/repair/inventory/selection/LevelGamePlayManager API signatures.
9. Safety policy approved for educational gameplay (not claimed as machine safety certification), evidence age rules, explicit independent W369 reset contract.
10. Full save/load persistence format with versioned manifest hash and monotonic evidence generation IDs.

When absent report **BLOCKED: UNSIGNED ELECTRICAL SCHEMATIC AND SENSOR/SUPERVISOR HARDWARE SPECIFICATION**. Do not invent approved pin functions or award objectives to conceal blockers.
